sec.title: Introduction
sec.p: Atopic dermatitis (AD) is a chronic inflammatory skin disease. 611, a humanized monoclonal antibody, selectively targets the interleukin (IL)-4 receptor alpha, thereby inhibiting the signaling of both interleukin (IL)-4 and IL-13. This phase 2 study aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of 611 in Chinese adults with moderate-to-severe AD.

sec.title: Methods
sec.p: This randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 2 study was conducted between October 2022 and September 2023. Eligible patients with moderate-to-severe AD were randomly assigned in a 1:1:1 ratio to receive 611 at a dose of either 300 mg (loading dose of 600 mg) every 2 weeks (Group A) or 300 mg (loading dose of 600 mg) every 4 weeks (Group B), or placebo every 2 weeks for 16 weeks, followed by an 8-week follow-up period. The primary efficacy endpoint was the proportion of patients achieving at least a 75% reduction in the Eczema Area and Severity Index (EASI-75) score at week 16. The safety and pharmacodynamics were also assessed.

sec.title: Results
sec.p: After 16 weeks of treatment, 60.0% of patients in Group A and 48.8% in Group B achieved EASI-75, both significantly higher than the placebo group (15.6%, p < 0.01). Additionally, 611 at both doses significantly improved the Investigator’s Global Assessment (IGA) scores, peak pruritus numerical rating scale (NRS), and other efficacy endpoints. Patients receiving 611 demonstrated significant reductions in serum thymus activation-regulated chemokine (TARC) and total serum immunoglobulin E (IgE) levels. The incidence of treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs) was similar across all dosage groups. The most common 611-related TEAE is upper respiratory tract infections. No new safety concerns were identified.

sec.title: Conclusion
sec.p: 611 demonstrated a high efficacy and a favorable safety profile in patients with moderate-to-severe AD.

tr.td: Atopic dermatitis (AD) is a chronic inflammatory skin disease with significant disease burden and limited treatment options for moderate-to-severe cases. An unmet need remains for novel biologic treatments that effectively target the underlying pathophysiology of AD while maintaining a favorable safety profile.
This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of 611, a humanized monoclonal antibody targeting interleukin-4 receptor alpha (IL-4Rα), in Chinese adults with moderate-to-severe AD.

Treatment with 611 demonstrated significant improvement in disease severity as measured by the Eczema Area and Severity Index (EASI-75), Investigator’s Global Assessment (IGA) 0/1 response, and reductions in pruritus and inflammatory biomarkers compared to placebo. The incidence of adverse events, including treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs) and serious adverse events (SAEs), was comparable across treatment and placebo groups, indicating a favorable safety profile.

This study supports the potential of 611 as an effective therapeutic option for moderate-to-severe AD and highlights the need for further investigation in diverse populations to confirm its long-term efficacy and safety.

sec.title: Introduction
sec.p: Atopic dermatitis (AD) is a chronic inflammatory skin disease characterized by eczematous lesions and intense pruritus. In Chinese adults, the 1-year prevalence of adult AD was 6.13%, and the point prevalence of AD was 2.42% [1]. The point prevalence of AD based on clinical diagnosis by dermatologists was 12.94% overall, ranging from 9.00% to 24.69% between metropolises for preschool children in China [2–4]. The pathogenesis of AD involves a complex interplay between environmental and genetic factors, resulting in immune dysregulation [5]. Major immune abnormalities include allergen presentation, T-helper 2 cell (Th2)-driven responses, impaired regulatory T cells, excessive immunoglobulin E (IgE) production, and increased eosinophils [6–10]. Type 2 inflammation, primarily mediated by interleukin (IL)−4 and IL-13, is thought to play a central role in AD pathogenesis [11]. Elevated IL-4 and IL-13 levels are associated with AD severity, facilitating IgE production, macrophage activation, eosinophil recruitment, and pruritus through IL-4Rα signaling in neurons [12].

Dupilumab, a fully human monoclonal antibody, targets the IL-4/IL-13 signaling to inhibit a major source of inflammation associated with AD. Since its approval in 2020 by the National Medical Products Administration (NMPA), dupilumab has been used to treat moderate-to-severe AD in China. 611 is a recombinant humanized immunoglobulin-G4 (IgG4) monoclonal antibody that inhibits IL-4 and IL-13 signaling. Preclinical and phase 1 clinical studies have validated the safety and tolerability of subcutaneous administration of 611 in healthy subjects. This phase 2 study aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of 611 in patients with moderate-to-severe AD.

sec.title: Study Design, Patients, and Treatment
sec.p: This multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 2 trial (ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT05544591) was conducted across 23 sites in China. This study adhered to the ethical principles of the Declaration of Helsinki for medical research involving human subjects and was conducted in accordance with Good Clinical Practice (GCP) guidelines. Before the study commenced, the clinical trial protocol, case report forms, informed consent forms, and other related documents were approved by the Peking University People’s Hospital Ethics Committee (approval number: 2022PHC022-001). All patients provided written informed consent for participation in the study. The study duration for each participant was 28 weeks, including a screening period of up to 4 weeks, a 16-week treatment period, and an 8-week follow-up period. Patients aged 18–75 years with moderate-to-severe AD were enrolled. Inclusion criteria included a baseline Investigator’s Global Assessment (IGA) score of ≥ 3, Eczema Area and Severity Index (EASI) score of ≥ 16, ≥ 10% body surface area (BSA) of AD involvement, and a weekly average peak pruritus numerical rating scale (NRS) score of ≥ 4. Detailed inclusion and exclusion criteria are outlined in Supplementary Table S1. After screening, eligible subjects were stratified by IGA scores (3 or 4) and randomly assigned in a 1:1:1 ratio to the following groups: Group A (611 300 mg every 2 weeks with a 600 mg loading dose), Group B (611 300 mg every 4 weeks with a 600 mg loading dose), or placebo. All participants used emollients at least 7 days before randomization and continued this regimen throughout the study.

sec.title: Efficacy Assessments
sec.p: The primary efficacy endpoint was the proportion of patients achieving at least a 75% reduction in the Eczema Area and Severity Index (EASI-75) score at week 16. Secondary endpoints included the proportion of participants achieving EASI-50, EASI-90, IGA score of 0 or 1 (0/1) with ≥ 2 point reduction, and ≥ 4 points or ≥ 3 points in the weekly average peak pruritus NRS score from baseline to week 16. The Dermatology Life Quality Index (DLQI) and Patient-Oriented Eczema Measure (POEM) were also evaluated. (A list of all efficacy endpoints is provided in Supplementary Table S2).

sec.title: Safety Assessments
sec.p: Safety assessment included treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs), vital signs, physical examinations, electrocardiograms (ECGs), and clinical laboratory test results.

sec.title: Biological Markers
sec.p: Pharmacodynamic markers included TARC, total serum IgE, peripheral blood eosinophil count (EOS), and lactate dehydrogenase (LDH).

sec.title: Statistical Analysis
sec.p: The sample size calculation was based on the primary endpoint (the percentage of subjects achieving an EASI-75 response at week 16). Assuming EASI-75 response rates of 49.2% for 611 and 11.5% for the placebo group at week 16, a sample size of 90 subjects with a randomization ratio of 1:1:1 was required to achieve a stated power of 80% to show superiority of 611 over placebo at a significance level of α = 0.05 (two-sided) accounting for a 10% dropout rate. The calculation is based on Fisher’s exact test for the binomial distribution using PASS 2019 software.

The primary analysis and binary endpoints were conducted in the Intent-to-Treat (ITT) analysis set, which included all randomized subjects, using the Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) test adjusted for stratification factors [baseline IGA score (3 or 4)] to compare the proportions of subjects between treatment groups. Intercurrent events, including the use of rescue therapy, administration of prohibited medications affecting the interpretation, or discontinuation of treatment due to lack of efficacy, were classified as non-responders from that time. Missing data were imputed using the non-responder imputation (NRI).

For continuous efficacy endpoints (e.g., a change from baseline in EASI score), an analysis of covariance (ANCOVA) model was employed to estimate the least square means (LSM) of changes from baseline to week 16 while controlling for baseline covariates and stratification factors. The intercurrent events, similar to the primary endpoint, were considered missing and imputed using the baseline observation carried forward (BOCF) from that time. Missing data were imputed using multiple imputation (MI), and the statistical inferences obtained from all imputed data were combined using Rubin’s rule. Safety analysis was conducted using descriptive statistics in the safety population, including all randomized subjects who received investigational drugs by treatment group.

sec.title: Baseline Characteristics
sec.p:
A total of 120 subjects were screened, and 30, 31, and 32 subjects were assigned to Group A, Group B, and the placebo group, respectively (Fig. 1). Nine patients withdrew from the study predominantly because of lack of efficacy (1 patient each in Groups A and B, and 7 patients in the placebo group).Fig. 1

A total of 120 patients were screened, with 93 randomized into three groups: Group A (611 300 mg every 2 weeks), Group B (611 300 mg every 4 weeks), and placebo. Nine patients discontinued the study because of lack of efficacy, predominantly in the placebo group

Demographics and baseline clinical characteristics, including gender, age, height, weight, and BMI, were well balanced across the treatment groups (Table 1). The proportion of subjects with an IGA score of 3 was 56.7%, 58.1%, and 56.3% in Group A, Group B, and the placebo group, respectively. The mean baseline EASI scores were 28.7, 26.2, and 28.6 in Group A, Group B, and the placebo group, respectively. sec.title: Efficacy Endpoints
sec.p:
At week 16, 60.0% patients in Group A and 48.4% patients in Group B achieved EASI-75, which were significantly higher than in the placebo group (15.6%, p < 0.01 for both comparisons with placebo) (Fig. 2A). Moreover, 33.3% patients in Group A and 29.0% patients in Group B achieved EASI-90, which were significantly higher than in the placebo group (9.4%, p < 0.05 for both comparisons with placebo). The LSM percentage changes in EASI scores from baseline to week 16 were − 69.2% (95% CI − 81.36%, − 57.06%) in Group A, − 68.5% (95% CI − 80.48%, − 56.47%) in Group B, and − 23.2% (95% CI − 34.86%, − 11.58%) in the placebo group (Fig. 2B).Fig. 2
Efficacy outcomes of 611 at week 16. A Proportion of patients achieving Eczema Area and Severity Index (EASI-75) in Group A, Group B, and placebo groups. Both Group A (60.0%) and Group B (48.4%) showed significantly higher response rates compared to placebo (15.6%; p < 0.01). B Least square mean (LSM) percentage change in EASI scores from baseline to week 16. Group A (− 69.2%; 95% CI − 81.36%, − 57.06%) and Group B (− 68.5%; 95% CI − 80.48%, − 56.47%) demonstrated significantly greater reductions compared to placebo (− 23.2%; 95% CI − 34.86%, − 11.58%). Data are presented as mean ± standard error

By week 16, the proportions of subjects achieving an IGA score of 0/1 with ≥ 2 point reduction from baseline were 33.3% in Group A and 35.5% in Group B, which were significantly higher than in the placebo group (9.4%, p < 0.05 for both comparisons with placebo) (Fig. 3A). The proportions of subjects achieving a ≥ 4-point reduction from baseline in the weekly average peak pruritus scores were 46.7% in group A and 45.2% in group B, which were significantly higher than in the placebo group (15.6%, p < 0.05 for both comparisons with placebo) (Fig. 3B). The LSM changes in DLQI scores from baseline to week 16 were − 4.8 (95% CI − 6.69, − 2.85), − 5.5 (95% CI − 7.30, − 3.79), and − 3.1 (95% CI − 4.83, − 1.44) for Group A, Group B, and the placebo group, respectively.Fig. 3
Improvements in Investigator’s Global Assessment (IGA) scores and peak pruritus numerical rating scale (NRS). A Proportion of patients achieving an IGA score of 0/1 with ≥ 2 point reduction from baseline. Group A (33.3%) and Group B (35.5%) exhibited significantly higher proportions compared to placebo (9.4%; p < 0.05). B Proportion of patients achieving ≥ 4-point reduction in weekly average peak pruritus NRS scores. Group A (46.7%) and Group B (45.2%) showed significant improvements versus placebo (15.6%; p < 0.05)

sec.title: Safety Endpoints
sec.p:
The incidence of TEAEs was similar between 611 and the placebo (63.3% in Group A and 64.5% in Group B vs. 65.6% in the placebo group), with most being TEAEs of Grades 1 or 2 severity (Table 2). In Group A, two subjects experienced Grade 3 TEAEs: one subject had elevated creatine phosphokinase levels, which normalized after reducing physical activity without treatment and was regarded as unrelated to 611. The other subject was found to have left lung cancer during the follow-up period post-treatment. It was regarded as unrelated to 611. In Group B, one subject experienced two Grade 3 TEAEs: the first event was pneumonia occurring during the treatment period, which improved after treatment and was regarded as unrelated to 611; the second event was dizziness, occurring during the safety follow-up period, which improved after treatment and was regarded as unrelated to 611.Table 2

The incidence of TEAEs associated with the investigational drug was slightly higher in both 611 treatment groups (26.7% and 16.1%) compared to the placebo group (12.5%), and the severity was all Grade 1 or 2. Upper respiratory tract infections were the most common treatment-related TEAEs in both 611 treatment groups, with 6.7% in group A and 3.2% in group B.
No significant abnormalities were detected in physical examinations, vital signs, ECGs, or laboratory tests across the three groups.

sec.title: Change in Biological Markers
sec.p: At week 16, the median percent reductions from baseline in TARC levels were 60.8%, 58.8%, and 28.9% in Group A, Group B, and the placebo group, respectively. Treatment with 611 resulted in a rapid and sustained reduction in TARC levels. By week 24, approximately 10–12 weeks after the last dose, TARC levels gradually returned to baseline values.

At week 16, the median percent reductions in total serum IgE levels were 49.7%, 36.6%, and 0% in Group A, Group B, and the placebo group, respectively. The total serum IgE levels showed a gradual decrease with treatment. No significant differences in EOS and LDH were detected between the 611 treatment and placebo groups.

sec.title: Discussion
sec.p: This study demonstrated that 611 was effective in patients with moderate-to-severe AD. The EASI-75, EASI-90, and IGA 0/1 in the two treatment groups were superior over the placebo group. The regimen of 600 mg + 300 mg Q2W showed a more robust and rapid response in achieving IGA 0/1, whereas the regimen of 600 mg + 300 mg Q4W exhibited comparable improvement at week 16. The 300 mg Q2W was selected as the preferred regimen during the core treatment period, whereas the 300 mg Q4W was adopted during the maintenance period in the Phase 3 clinical trial (NCT06173284).

Subjects receiving treatment with 611 showed notable improvements in itch symptoms as early as week 2, with 10% and 16.1% of subjects in Groups A and B achieving an NRS score ≥ 4, which was similar to those of the dupilumab Q2W group (9% ~ 11% [13]). By week 4, 23.3% and 12.9% of subjects in Groups A and B achieved an NRS score ≥ 4 (dupilumab Q2W: 16%–23% [13]). By week 16, 46.7% and 45.2% of subjects in Groups A and B, respectively, achieved an NRS score ≥ 4 (dupilumab Q2W: 36% ~ 41% [13]). Overall, receiving 611 every other week demonstrated similar efficacy to dupilumab in relieving patients’ symptoms. The incidence of rescue therapy was significantly lower in 611 treatment groups compared to the placebo group. The proportions of subjects who had used rescue therapy at least once were 16.7% (5/30), 12.9% (4/31), and 31.3% (10/32) in Group A, B, and placebo, respectively.

Common adverse reactions associated with dupilumab in clinical studies for atopic dermatitis include injection site reactions (including erythema, edema, pruritus, pain, and inflammation), conjunctivitis, allergic conjunctivitis, arthralgia, oral herpes, and eosinophilia. In this study, only 1.6% of subjects treated with 611 experienced injection site reactions and injection site erythema related to the experimental drug (vs. dupilumab SOLO 1 and SOLO 2—injection site reactions: 8%–19%), and 1.6% of subjects treated with 611 experienced allergic conjunctivitis (vs. dupilumab SOLO 1 and SOLO 2—conjunctivitis: 3%–5%); all of the above were significantly lower than those found in SOLO 1 and SOLO 2. The lower incidence of conjunctivitis observed with 611 compared to dupilumab may be attributed to differences in molecular structure, binding affinity, or immune modulation beyond IL-4Rα inhibition. While both 611 and dupilumab target IL-4Rα, subtle variations in pharmacokinetics and immunogenicity may contribute to differences in adverse event profiles. Further investigations, including comparative clinical and mechanistic studies, are necessary to elucidate the underlying reasons for these observed differences.

TARC and IgE are biological markers indicative of type 2 inflammation [14]. 611 demonstrated a significant effect on the decrease of TARC and IgE levels. This finding further supports the specific mechanism of action of 611 in inhibiting IL-4 and IL-13 signaling pathways. Changes in EOS and LDH were minimal and showed a weak correlation with clinical improvements.

AD exhibits genetic and phenotypic variations across different populations. Several studies have reported that East Asian patients with AD, including those in China, often present with unique clinical features, such as a higher prevalence of lichenification, the highest levels of TH17/TH22 activation among all ethnic groups, higher serum IgE levels compared to European populations, and a higher frequency of filaggrin gene mutations than African populations, which are closely associated with impaired skin barrier function [15]. These genetic and phenotypic differences may contribute to variations in AD pathogenesis and treatment responses. Furthermore, studies have shown that Asian patients with AD exhibit more pronounced type 2 and type 17 inflammatory responses, which may influence therapeutic efficacy [16]. Therefore, although the efficacy and safety of 611 in Chinese patients align with global findings on IL-4Rα inhibitors, further investigations in diverse populations are necessary to establish its broader applicability.

While this study provides valuable insights into the efficacy and safety of 611 in Chinese adults with moderate-to-severe AD, several limitations should be considered. First, this study was conducted exclusively in a Chinese adult population, which may limit the generalizability of the findings to other ethnic groups. Further research is needed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of 611 in a more diverse global population, including pediatric patients. Second, the relatively short follow-up period (16 weeks of treatment plus an 8-week follow-up period) restricts the ability to assess the long-term efficacy and safety of 611, particularly regarding potential adverse events that may emerge with prolonged use. Two ongoing Phase 3 studies with a 52-week treatment period are currently being conducted to further evaluate the long-term efficacy and safety of 611. Finally, while the study assessed key clinical endpoints such as EASI-75, IGA 0/1, and pruritus reduction, further investigation is required to determine the broader applicability of 611 in clinical practice.

sec.title: Conclusion
sec.p: 611 showed good efficacy and favorable safety profiles in Chinese adults with moderate-to-severe AD, achieving significant improvements across multiple efficacy endpoints compared to the placebo group. The results of this Phase 2 study underscore the potential of 611 as an IL-4Rα antibody for treating AD in adult patients, offering a promising new therapeutic option for those with moderate-to-severe AD.
